title: Akureyri: Lake Mývatn, Goðafoss & Lava Fields Cruise Tour
desc: Discover the dramatic volcanic landscapes surrounding Lake Mývatn on this unforgettable shore excursion from Akureyri. This tour has been carefully designed for cruise passengers, allowing you to experience some of North Iceland’s most spectacular natural wonders within a comfortable timeframe.  Your journey begins with a scenic drive from Akureyri through the beautiful northern countryside. The first stop is  Ljósavatn , a peaceful lake offering a quick photo opportunity and a chance to enjoy the tranquil Icelandic scenery.  Next, you will visit one of Iceland’s most iconic waterfalls,  Goðafoss - the Waterfall of the Gods . Here you’ll have time to walk along the viewing paths, take photos and admire the powerful turquoise water cascading into the canyon below.  Continuing towards the Lake Mývatn region, you will explore the  Skútustaðagígar pseudo-craters , unique volcanic formations created by steam explosions thousands of years ago. The area offers beautiful panoramic views over the lake and surrounding landscapes.  The tour continues to  Dimmuborgir , often called the “Dark Castles”, where dramatic lava formations create a mysterious maze of towers, caves and arches. This stop also includes time for lunch, with local restaurants and cafés available nearby.  Another scenic stop is  Grjótagjá , a small lava cave with a geothermal hot spring inside. The crystal blue water and volcanic surroundings make this a fascinating and photogenic location. Visitors are asked to respect the fragile environment and keep the area clean.  Before returning to Akureyri, you will experience the otherworldly terrain known as the  Fly Lands , where geothermal activity and volcanic forces have shaped a landscape unlike anywhere else in Iceland.  After a day filled with natural wonders, you will relax on the drive back to Akureyri with plenty of time before your ship’s departure.

title: Blue Ice Cave Exploration from Jökulsárlón (Small Group Tour)
desc: You will get the opportunity of a lifetime to enjoy one of the world’s greatest wilderness, Iceland’s largest glacier. You are driven in a specially modified car to the glacier, where you get to explore the glacier environment, enjoy a view out of this world, go into and underneath the glacier, and experience the glacier’s beauty from the inside! The Blue Ice Cave Exploration is truly a unique experience.   An experienced local guide leads the way and shares a wealth of fascinating information about glaciers, icefields, and their impact on our environment during our journey, making sure everyone enjoys themselves to the fullest. Our guides provide you with safety equipment (helmet and crampons) and the fun begins!       We also offer the option for guidance in Chinese (based on availability).      Looking for a private tour of the Ice Cave? Click   here   .        Disclaimer:  Please note that the images provided are for reference only. As the ice cave is a natural phenomenon, its appearance changes constantly throughout the season. Therefore, the actual ice cave this year may differ from the images shown. Sometimes, the colour of the cave might be darker due to lack of sunlight or there might be small flood in the cave due to rain, these are natural occurance and cannot be basis of refund dispute.  The 3 hour tour duration includes driving time to and from the glacier, hiking time to and from the cave, and time inside the cave.

title: Chasing Totality: Iceland Solar Eclipse Expedition 2026
desc: Join us for a once-in-a-lifetime Icelandic expedition into the path of totality during the Total Solar Eclipse of August 12th, 2026. As the moon’s shadow moves across the North Atlantic, we will leave Reykjavík behind and journey through Iceland’s dramatic landscapes in search of the best possible eclipse viewing conditions.Our primary destination is the breathtaking Snæfellsnes Peninsula, a region known for its volcanic coastlines, rugged sea cliffs, lava fields, glacier views, and raw Icelandic beauty. With landmarks such as Lóndrangar rising above the Atlantic Ocean, the peninsula offers a truly unforgettable backdrop for one of nature’s rarest events.Because Icelandic weather can change rapidly, this experience is designed as a weather-adaptive eclipse expedition rather than a fixed sightseeing itinerary. Our operations team will continuously monitor cloud and weather forecasts before departure to maximize the chances of clear eclipse visibility. Depending on conditions, the route may be adjusted toward another carefully selected viewing area within the path of totality, including regions along Iceland’s South Coast or Reykjanes Peninsula.Departing Reykjavík early in the morning, this full-day experience is built around comfortably positioning ourselves for the eclipse rather than rushing between attractions. Once we reach the selected viewing area, guests will have time to relax, take in the surrounding scenery, enjoy picnic-style refreshments, and fully embrace the unique atmosphere leading up to totality.Guests will also have the opportunity to explore the surrounding landscape on foot, including an optional scenic walk toward the dramatic coastal cliffs of Lóndrangar, located approximately 30 minutes from the viewing area.As daylight slowly fades and the temperature drops, witness the surreal moment when the moon completely covers the sun and Iceland briefly falls into twilight beneath the glowing solar corona. For many travelers, a total solar eclipse is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Experiencing it surrounded by Iceland’s wild landscapes makes it even more extraordinary.This tour includes transportation from Reykjavík, eclipse viewing glasses, picnic-style refreshments, and guidance from our experienced local team throughout the journey.Please note that eclipse visibility cannot be guaranteed due to weather conditions, and the route or viewing location may change on the day of departure in order to provide the best possible viewing experience.

title: Classic Whales & Viking Horses
desc: Start your day with a complimentary pickup at your accommodation around 9:30. The adventure starts with a small-group horse riding tour, where you'll get to know the unique Icelandic horse while exploring stunning landscapes. After a short riding lesson, ride through the forest at Hólmsheiði hill and past the striking lava formations of Rauðhólar. The total riding time is between 1,5-2 hrs. and ends at the stables with a warm drink before Viking Horses drops you off at Reykjavík’s Old Harbour for the next part of your journey.  Set sail into Faxaflói bay in the early afternoon, with our expert crew and marine biologist guides. Under the guidance of passionate naturalists, discover the incredible whales of Reykjavík, from humpbacks and minke whales to white-beaked dolphins and harbour porpoises. The bay is also teeming with birdlife, including puffins, northern gannets, and arctic terns. Whether in summer or winter, every tour offers a chance to witness Iceland’s rich marine life against a breathtaking backdrop. After the tour you can make your own way into the city for a lovely afternoon in town, or you can request a drop off back to your hotel (additional fee).

Designed specifically for cruise ship passengers, this tour is carefully timed to match your ship’s schedule, ensuring a smooth and stress-free experience with guaranteed return to port no later than 1 hour before your ship’s departure.  Your adventure begins with a scenic coastal drive through the remote and beautiful landscapes of East Iceland. The highlight of the tour is the incredible Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon, one of Iceland’s most iconic destinations. The itinerary is carefully planned with cruise schedules in mind, allowing sufficient time at each stop while ensuring a comfortable return to Ísafjörður well before your ship’s departure. title: Glacier Hike, South Coast Waterfalls & Black Sand Beach
desc: Experience what it is like to stand on a glacier  Embark on a remarkable day trip from Reykjavik to explore Iceland’s enchanting south coast. Delve into the magic of the Sólheimajökull glacier as you gear up for an exciting glacier hike, equipped with harnesses, crampons, ice picks, and helmets.  Discover iconic attractions like stunning waterfalls and the world-renowned Reynisfjara black-sand beach. These natural wonders encapsulate the unique beauty of Iceland’s south coast, making this journey an unforgettable experience.  Don't miss out on this captivating adventure!    Itinerary   Glacier Hike on Sólheimajökull Sólheimajökull, an outlet glacier of Mýrdalsjökull, Iceland’s fourth-largest glacier, graces the South Coast with its presence. Located just 158 kilometers (98 miles) from Reykjavík, it offers a unique opportunity to explore glacial features and gain insight into its formation. This icy realm is a living testament to the dynamic forces that shape Iceland’s ever-changing landscape.   The Black Sand Beach  Reynisfjara, a stunning black sand beach on the South Coast, showcases the raw power of the Atlantic Ocean. Its colossal waves crash upon the shore, creating an awe-inspiring spectacle. Basalt columns, resembling ancient sentinels, line the beach, while the enigmatic “Reynisdrangar” sea stacks emerge from the ocean’s depths, steeped in local folklore. This beach has earned its place among the world’s most beautiful non-tropical beaches.   Skogafoss waterfall Skogafoss, one of Iceland’s classic waterfalls, stands as a magnificent testament to the power of nature. Soaring to a height of 65 meters and spanning 25 meters in width, it ranks among the country’s largest waterfalls. Local legend weaves tales of a hidden chest of gold behind the falls, a challenge that would require the strength and bravery of a Viking to pursue.   Seljalandsfoss waterfalls Seljalandsfoss, another of Iceland’s classic waterfalls, offers a unique twist on the traditional waterfall experience. While not among the country’s largest falls, what sets Seljalandsfoss apart is the rare opportunity to walk behind the cascading water for most of the year. This immersive encounter transports you into a world of mist and magic, revealing a different perspective of nature’s beauty.

title: Golden Circle Day Tour with Local Surprise - Small Group Minibus
desc: Experience Iceland’s most famous sightseeing route, the  Golden Circle , in a comfortable  small-group minibus  with an experienced English-speaking guide.  This full-day tour takes you to three of Iceland’s most iconic natural attractions. Your first stop is  Þingvellir National Park , a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates slowly drift apart. The park is also one of the most historically significant places in Iceland, as it was the site of the country’s first parliament.  Next, you will visit the  Geysir geothermal area , home to bubbling hot springs and the famous  Strokkur geyser , which erupts every few minutes and sends hot water up to 20–30 meters into the air. title: Grundarfjörður Cruise Tour: Snæfellsnes Peninsula with Local Surprise
desc: Experience the wonders of the Snæfellsnes Peninsula on a delightful shore excursion designed just for cruise guests arriving at Grundarfjörður Port. Our friendly team keeps a close eye on ship timetables to make sure you return to your ship comfortably and on time, making your day fun and worry-free. You’ll then travel along the scenic Snæfellsnes coastline, stopping at breathtaking viewpoints, unique volcanic beaches, and historic fishing villages that truly capture the spirit of Iceland. Throughout your tour, your knowledgeable local guide will share fun stories, interesting history, and fascinating facts about Icelandic nature and everyday life, making your experience both educational and memorable for the whole family. With comfortable transportation, carefully timed stops, and unforgettable scenery, this Snæfellsnes shore excursion is a fantastic way for families to discover the magic of Iceland during your cruise visit to Grundarfjörður.

title: Hvammsvík Hot Spring with bus transfer from and to Reykjavík
desc: Hvammsvík Hot Springs is the #1 place to visit in the world according to Timeout       Take a short 45-minute bus ride from Reykjavik. Pick up from multiple hotels available 30 minutes earlier.       An ever-changing experience. In harmony with the tides and seasons.   What's unique about Hvammsvik Hot Springs is that they are part of a 1200 acre private estate that offers you complete freedom to explore and experience all our surroundings far away from the city life yet only a 45 minute picturesque drive from Reykjavik.  You will find yourself immersed in perfectly warm hot springs all year round right on the edge of the ocean.  In fact some of our hot springs will actually fill up as they are submerged in high tide giving you and ever changing experience.   Recharge, naturally!  We offer eight natural hot springs of varying temperatures, a steam cave and outdoor relaxation areas. We have brand new facilities yet inspired by history of Hvammsvik that dates back to the 12th century.  You can even try out our outdoor changing facilities where you will shower under the open sky.  An exploration of Hvammsvík Hot Springs will leave you both relaxed and invigorated.   Pure, Salty and Good   At Hvammsvík Hot Springs you are immersed in a perfect fusion of geothermal water, flowing from our very own source 1400 meters underground, with seawater straight from the Atlantic ocean. The steady stream of this unique blend of water, between pools, over their edges and back into the ocean, ensures optimum water quality and cleanliness.  After a soak in the Hot Springs we recommend you try some delicious, light dishes inspired by our surroundings at our bistro. The seafood soup is a favorite or our infamous algae/ginger shot!  Come immerse yourself in unfiltered Icelandic nature, only 45 minutes from Reykjavík city center.   In harmony with nature   Our aim at Hvammsvik Hot Springs is to give our guests an authentic Icelandic nature experience. The area is rich in local wildlife, with over 30 different types of birds that reside in and around Hvammsvik. Wild sheep roam around in the summer and if lucky you might spot an Arctic Fox. Quite a few elves are said to reside in the rocks and hills of the nature resort!  Hvammsvík has its share of spectacular northern lights. Best time to witness the aurora borealis is in the evenings from October through April. Should you not witness the northern lights while soaking in the pools this is the perfect tour to combo with a northern lights evening tour.   A place in History   Hvammsvík is a historical landmark that was first discovered by the Vikings 1000 years ago, as recorded in Landnáma, the Icelandic book of settlers dating back to the 11th century. No wonder they chose Hvammsvík, given its incredible landscape, natural harbour, geothermal heat and wildlife.

title: Ice Cave & Glacier Hike with South Coast Waterfalls
desc: Step into a world of ice and wonder  Your adventure begins on Sólheimajökull, an outlet glacier of mighty Mýrdalsjökull, Iceland’s fourth-largest ice cap. After gearing up with crampons, harness, helmet, and ice axe, you’ll set foot on the glacier and explore crevasses, ridges, and ever-changing ice formations.  The highlight of the day awaits as you venture inside a natural ice cave, where shimmering blue walls and frozen sculptures reveal the glacier’s hidden heart. Standing within this otherworldly cathedral of ice is an unforgettable experience.  After the glacier adventure, the journey continues with visits to two of Iceland’s most iconic waterfalls.  Skógafoss , thundering 65 meters down from ancient sea cliffs, is both breathtaking and steeped in legend. Further west lies  Seljalandsfoss , where you can walk behind the falling curtain of water for a magical perspective.   This full-day tour combines glacier hiking, ice cave exploration, and stunning waterfalls for an adventure that captures the very essence of Iceland’s natural beauty.    Itinerary   Glacier Hike & Natural Ice Cave on Sólheimajökull  Sólheimajökull, an outlet glacier of Mýrdalsjökull, Iceland’s fourth-largest glacier, graces the South Coast with its presence. Located just 158 kilometers (98 miles) from Reykjavík, it offers a unique opportunity to explore striking glacial features and gain insight into their formation. This icy realm is a living testament to the powerful, ever-changing forces that shape Iceland’s landscape.  At the Sólheimajökull parking lot, you gear up with crampons, helmet, harness and ice axe, and step onto the ice. Hike across ridges, crevasses, and a glacier lagoon while learning how these formations are created. Then venture into the glacier’s ice cave—an otherworldly chamber of vivid blue ice and natural wonder.   Skogafoss waterfall  Skogafoss, one of Iceland’s classic waterfalls, stands as a magnificent testament to the power of nature. Soaring to a height of 65 meters and spanning 25 meters in width, it ranks among the country’s largest waterfalls. Local legend weaves tales of a hidden chest of gold behind the falls, a challenge that would require the strength and bravery of a Viking to pursue.   Seljalandsfoss waterfalls  Seljalandsfoss, another of Iceland’s classic waterfalls, offers a unique twist on the traditional waterfall experience. While not among the country’s largest falls, what sets Seljalandsfoss apart is the rare opportunity to walk behind the cascading water for most of the year. This immersive encounter transports you into a world of mist and magic, revealing a different perspective of nature’s beauty.

title: Landmannalaugar Highlands 4x4 Minibus Tour with Hot Spring Bath
desc: Leave behind the buzz of the city and set your sights on the untamed heart of Iceland! This full-day 4x4 adventure plunges you into the wild Highlands, where the geothermal marvels of  Landmannalaugar  await.  Accessible only during the summer months, Landmannalaugar is cut off for most of the year due to snow-covered mountain roads, making it one of Iceland’s most exclusive destinations. Widely considered the most beautiful place in Iceland, its landscapes truly look like something straight out of a fantasy movie. Take time to explore this natural fortress before pressing onward to the thunderous heights of  Háifoss , one of the tallest waterfalls in the country - a place that looks like something straight out of  Stranger Things .  Then, discover  Sigöldufoss , a stunning Highland waterfall set in a remote and surreal landscape.  Braving rugged Highland roads, your 4x4 powers through to  Landmannalaugar , a legendary realm of rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains and bubbling geothermal springs.   Here, adventure is at its peak:  trek a scenic 5 km hike (moderate level) through otherworldly terrain -  proper hiking boots are essential  - then soak your trail-weary muscles in a steaming natural hot spring, surrounded by towering peaks.  But the adventure doesn’t end there. On your return, stop at  Hnausapollur crater,  a remote volcanic lake that dwarfs Kerið in both size and mystique. Then, marvel at  Sigöldugljúfur canyon , often referred to as the “ Valley of Tears ,” where countless waterfalls cascade into a magical gorge carved by time.  A final comfort stop lets you catch your breath before you roll back into Reykjavik, your spirit awakened and your memory brimming with wild Icelandic tales. title: Reykjavík Classic Whale Watching including pickup
desc: Enjoy a magical journey into Faxaflói bay with our expert crew and specially trained naturalists. Explore the whales of Reykjavík under the excellent guidance of our marine biologist guides and learn all about the incredible wildlife that call Iceland their home. The bay is even full of   birdlife  , from puffins and gannets to guillemots and more, that actively feed on the plentiful fish found in the bay. Magnificent landscapes surround the area and add a unique contrast to the vast ocean, where the spectacular views on the horizon are certainly not to be missed.   Meet us at our   ticket office     by the Old Harbour in downtown Reykjavík, where you will exchange your pre-paid voucher for boarding tickets. A few steps down the pier you will find our Visitor Centre, facilitated on board a converted fishing vessel permanently placed by the pier. This is where you will meet crew. Head downstairs to the hull of the boat and stroll through our unique floating   wildlife exhibition     to learn more about the animals we may come across on our tours.   You board the whale watching boat through the Visitor Centre, where you will find several outdoor viewing platforms, a heated indoor saloon with large viewing windows, a cafeteria where you can buy light refreshments, toilet facilities and a cloak room where you can borrow our blankets and overalls for the duration of the tour. You can stay outside in the fresh air but you are also welcome to settle inside the heated lounge and observe from within. One of our excellent naturalists will give a live commentary throughout the tour and notify you of any sightings as we go.  The most   common whale species   encountered on our tours are the minke whales, humpback whales, white-beaked dolphins and harbour porpoises. Occasionally we see other species such as killer whales, fin whales, sei whales and long-finned pilot whales, however they are not as common. The whales are most abundant in summer, giving us a great chance to enjoy and understand them in their natural environment. Each year continues to surprise us however with the variety of whales we see in winter, and as our   research     shows, more and more whales are staying in the area all year round!  This tour option includes pick up / drop off to your hotel or nearby bus stop. Please confirm your hotel no later than 48 hrs. before departure.   Combine this activity with     Puffin Watching         in the summer or with a     Northern Lights Cruise     in winter! You can also check out some of the     other combo tours         we have put together!

title: South Coast - Plane Wreck, Bird watching &Glacier hike冰岛南岸飞机残骸,观鸟&冰川中文一日中巴团
desc: 清晨从雷克雅未克启程向南，我们将带您驶入一场关于风、海与火山的长日旅途。夏季的冰岛，白昼悠长，时间仿佛被温柔地拉伸，让每一处风景都多停留一会儿。一日行程大约11-12小时。  第一站，是荒原深处的 Sólheimasandur飞机残骸。摆渡车缓缓驶过无边的黑沙，天地之间只剩下风声与脚步的回响。那架银色的机身静静躺在大地之上，像一段被遗忘的故事，也像时间在此刻凝固。你可以走近它、触摸它，在极简的世界里，感受一种孤独而辽阔的美。  随后来到海风猎猎的 Dyrhólaey海岬。这里是海鸟的乐园，夏日里，海鹦在悬崖间穿梭飞翔。脚下是汹涌的大西洋，远处是拱门状的海蚀岩，浪花在黑沙之上反复书写与抹去，像一首永不停歇的诗。  午后走向不远处的 雷尼斯黑沙滩。黑色的沙粒、几何般排列的玄武岩柱、以及远方海中矗立的岩石——传说那是被阳光定格的巨人。海浪一阵阵涌来，带着不可预测的力量，也带着一种原始而纯粹的美。  接下来，是属于探险者的时刻（英文项目）：踏上 Sólheimajökull索尔黑马冰川，在冰与时间雕刻的纹理之上缓缓前行，听见脚下冰川的呼吸。  傍晚时分，Hvolsvöllur小镇可以短暂休整。夏日的光仍未褪去，晚餐在柔和的光线中展开，空气中带着海的气息与旅途的余温。  归途上，天色缓慢地变化，却迟迟不肯真正落下。车窗外的山影与海岸渐渐远去，而这一天的风景，却会在记忆中停留很久很久。

title: Vik to Katla Ice Cave Adventure: Explore Iceland's Frozen Wonders
desc: Mýrdalsjökull glacier is renowned as one of Iceland's most iconic landmarks, and it's the source of the captivating Kötlujökull glacier. title: Walk with a Viking - Reykjavik Walking Tour - Small group
desc: YOUR CRASH COURSE IN EVERYTHING ICELANDIC  Our Reykjavik walking tour is your introduction to our country. It will help you get your bearings and make the most of your stay in Iceland.   We recommend it as your first stop in Reykjavik (well, maybe check into your accommodation and drop your bags off first).  Our family-friendly tour brings the history of Iceland to life with exciting stories and Icelandic mythology.  We’ll visit all of the famous landmarks in the city center, such as Harpa Concert Hall, Reykjavik Harbour, and Hallgrímskirkja Church (we’ll teach you how to pronounce that), Reykjavik Pond, and the Parliament building.   But, we’ll also share hidden, local spots with you like a visit to an Elf home; things you’d miss if you didn’t know what to look for.  We want you to feel the unique, friendly atmosphere of our quirky little city, not just to see the most popular tourist attractions. We’ll even have a small lesson on the Icelandic language so you can not only walk with a Viking but talk like one too.  We’ll be showing you our favorite places to eat, drink and visit (we also have an intimate knowledge of happy hour deals that we’re happy to share).
